title: Corporate wireless for a branch office
scenario: Northwind Logistics is bringing a new branch office online. Configure the corporate access point to meet the requirements below. Every setting is scored independently, so complete every field even if you are unsure of one.
requirements: Employees authenticate with their own corporate identity. When someone leaves the company, revoking that one account must remove their wireless access without affecting anyone else.
The internal PKI has already issued client certificates to every corporate laptop. Authentication must be mutual, with both the client and the server proving identity by certificate.
An attacker who captures the wireless association must not be able to crack the credential offline.
Users in the warehouse are being repeatedly knocked off the network by forged frames. Stop this.
The access point must not offer any setup shortcut that bypasses the configured authentication.
Apply only controls that provide real security. Do not add configuration that provides obscurity and ongoing administrative cost without stopping an attacker.
The RADIUS server is at 10.10.5.20 and uses the current IANA assigned authentication port.

subtasks.label: Authentication mode
subtasks.correctNote: Per user identity plus individual revocation means 802.1X, and the offline cracking requirement rules out WPA2. WPA3-Enterprise is the only mode that satisfies both.

subtasks.label: EAP method
subtasks.correctNote: Client certificates are already deployed and the requirement says mutual certificate authentication. That is EAP-TLS and nothing else.

subtasks.label: RADIUS server address
subtasks.correctNote: The scenario gives the address directly. Enterprise mode is unusable without it.

subtasks.label: RADIUS port
subtasks.correctNote: 1812 is RADIUS authentication. 1813 is RADIUS accounting, 1645 is the legacy pre-standard port, 49 is TACACS+ and 389 is LDAP.

subtasks.label: Protected Management Frames
subtasks.correctNote: Forged frames knocking users off the network is a deauthentication attack. PMF set to required is the control that stops it, and WPA3 mandates it.

subtasks.label: WPS
subtasks.correctNote: WPS is the setup shortcut that bypasses your authentication design. Disable it.

subtasks.label: SSID broadcast
subtasks.correctNote: Hiding the SSID is obscurity, not security, and it degrades roaming. The requirement explicitly excluded controls of this kind.

subtasks.label: MAC filtering
subtasks.correctNote: MAC addresses are trivially spoofed and the filter list is a permanent administrative burden. Same exclusion as SSID hiding.
